entries.text: Thank you for calling VeloFit. Your call may be monitored or recorded for quality assurance. Please say or press 1 for questions about an existing order. Press 2 for new product inquiries.
One.
Connecting you to the next available agent.
Thank you for calling VeloFit, my name is Alex. How can I help you today?
Hi, I need to start a return for an item I bought recently. It's the VeloBand Pulse.
I can certainly help you with that. Can I get your name and order number, please?
Sure, the name is Sam Jones, and the order number is VF789012.
Thank you, Sam. One moment... Okay, I see the order. The VeloBand Pulse, delivered 11 days ago. Yes, you're well within our 90-day return window, so we can definitely get that started for you.
Oh, 90 days? That's fantastic! I was worried I was pushing it. Thanks for making it so easy.
Not a problem at all. Let me just generate the... wait a second. Oh. Sam, I am so sorry, I need to correct myself.
Correct yourself? What do you mean?
I was looking at the policy for our apparel line. My apologies. For electronics like the VeloBand Pulse, the return policy is actually 30 days, not 90.
Wait, what? But **you just said** it was 90 days. I heard you clearly.
I know I did, and that was my mistake. I deeply apologize for the confusion. You still have 19 days to make the return, so you are still well within the correct window.
I don't think you understand. You **promised me** 90 days. This feels like a classic **bait and switch**. You tell me one thing to make me happy and then pull it away.
Sir, it was an honest mistake, not an attempt to mislead you. The policy is firm at 30 days for this item.
This is a **recorded line**, isn't it? You can't just make a promise and then pretend it didn't happen. I expect you to honor what you told me. I want the 90 days.
I understand your frustration, but my system will not physically allow me to process a return for this item category after 30 days. I cannot override the policy.
Then get me someone who can. This is unacceptable. I want to speak to your supervisor. Now.
Of course. Please hold one moment while I transfer you.
Hello, my name is Maria, I'm a supervisor here at VeloFit. I've been briefed on the situation regarding the return window. How can I help?
Your agent, Alex, told me I had 90 days to return my VeloBand Pulse. Now he's saying it's 30. I want you to honor what your employee told me on this recorded call.

I want to start by sincerely apologizing for the incorrect information you received. That was a significant error on our part and I will be addressing it with the agent. However, our company-wide policy for all electronic devices is, and has always been, 30 days.
So you're admitting your agent was wrong, but you're still not going to do anything about it? What is the point of recording calls for 'quality assurance' if you don't assure any quality?

I understand your position, and you're right to be upset. While I cannot extend the return window to 90 days, I can offer you a $25 store credit for the severe inconvenience and the miscommunication you experienced.

A $25 credit? That's an insult. This isn't about $25, it's about your company not honoring its word. This is unresolved. You haven't helped at all. I'll just make sure my review online is very, very specific.
I am truly sorry we couldn't find a resolution that was satisfactory for you, Sam. Is there anything else at all?
No. Goodbye.
